injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce an ongoing fault or a device “reboot loop.” End-to-end reachability is clean (0% loss, ~1.4 ms RTT between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1). All BGP adjacencies across the fabric are Established and stable. Host uptimes are ~3h55m on every router and host, so no boxes are actually rebooting.

What did happen very recently is a control-plane restart: on every router (including the “switch near the other rack,” leaf_router_0_1), FRR daemons (bgpd/zebra) show start time Sat Aug 8 12:56:02 UTC, and BGP neighbors report Up/Down ≈ 2 minutes with “Peer has restarted (R/N bit set).” The FRR log on leaf_router_0_1 and both spines shows fresh initialization at 12:56:03–05. That would have dropped BGP sessions briefly and could have felt like a “switch reboot” and caused a short cross‑rack flap, but it was a one‑time event; there is no evidence of repeated cycles since then.

Localization: FRR services (not the hardware) on all routers restarted around 12:56 UTC. Interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 (eth0/1/2) are up; no link up/down events are logged, and frr.service is active. Root cause: a recent FRR service restart across the fabric (trigger unknown from available logs).

Corrective fix: no immediate action required; connectivity is stable now. To prevent future surprises, review automation/timers that may restart frr (cron/systemd), and consider setting frr.service Restart=on-failure instead of always if unintended restarts are suspected. Monitor frr.log for new restarts.
